NextItNet uses left-padded histories and causal residual convolutions. Its reference implementation pads each causal convolution by (kernel_size−1)×dilation on the left and reads the final sequence position for inference. Derived correctness tests: perturb tokens strictly after several intermediate positions t and require unchanged features and candidate logits through t; repeat in evaluation and deterministic training modes. Compute dependency sets across every convolution, composing offsets along sequential paths and taking unions at residual additions. For stride-one stacks, maximum receptive-field width is 1+Σ(kernel_size−1)×dilation over the longest path, including both convolutions in two-convolution blocks. Test invariance outside that boundary and demonstrate sensitivity at reachable boundary positions with controlled weights, avoiding accidental zero gradients. Include short, heavily padded histories; verify padding embeddings/masking follow the intended contract and readout selects the final nonpadding index, never count−1. These are testing recommendations derived from the [reference architecture](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html).

Feature-extraction causality alone does not establish deployed correctness. Load the actual exported predictor and checkpoint; compare its candidate scores with DiagnosisProbe/ModelView scoring for identical histories, item IDs, truncation, padding and category routing. Check numerical agreement and ranking, including singleton and batched requests. Normalization axes require explicit audit: BatchNorm1d on B×C×L pools statistics across batch and time during training, leaking future information; evaluation also uses batch statistics when running statistics are disabled. InstanceNorm and GroupNorm on temporal tensors likewise aggregate across positions; LayerNorm can leak when its normalized dimensions include time. Channel-only LayerNorm on B×L×C preserves positional independence. See [BatchNorm documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.batchnorm.BatchNorm1d.html) and the reference implementation’s channel-only normalization.
